title: Bound filesystem reads and paginate directory and instruction search results before allocation
outcome: Filesystem and instruction APIs avoid unbounded reads, match lists and directory enumeration responses while retaining exact content access.
acceptance: File reads enforce the existing10MiB limit during the actual read, including growth after stat; instruction graph/file/match processing has explicit byte and work budgets.

Directory entries, instruction matches and agent-command catalogs use bounded pages/projections with explicit continuation/completeness; long lines and command templates cannot create unbounded result records.
Existing file/command resolution and authorization owners are reused; content remains accessible through bounded reads and no filesystem content is truncated or changed by browsing.
Tests cover growth races, large directories, long lines and escaped content using small fixtures; independent review and full gate pass.
